business_problem: Autonomous-driving teams need large volumes of precise, machine-readable traffic scenarios for virtual validation and homologation, but writing standardized scenario descriptions is tedious, repetitive, and dependent on scarce domain experts.
solution_summary: DXC-Luxoft built scenARI.Lux as a generative AI chatbot application for autonomous-driving validation. The system ingests human-readable traffic situation descriptions and routes them through multiple bots coordinated by a dedicated agent application so the workflow can support different LLM foundation models. To improve answer quality and latency, the pipeline uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation, feeding OpenX standards definitions into the process as an authoritative knowledge base. DXC-Luxoft also fine-tunes the underlying model with manually created scenarios and, optionally, client scenarios. The application generates ASAM OpenDRIVE and ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL/XML outputs that simulators can execute, turning free-text inputs into standardized scenario artifacts for virtual testing. DXC-Luxoft positions those generated scenarios as inputs to its broader autonomous-driving validation toolchain, including collaboration with MicroVision for real-world scenario abstraction.

data_flow: Human-readable traffic descriptions are submitted to scenARI.Lux, where multiple bots coordinated by a dedicated agent application process the input with LLMs. RAG injects OpenX standards definitions, and fine-tuning on manually created and optional client scenarios improves generation. The system then emits ASAM OpenDRIVE and ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL/XML files for simulators and downstream virtual-validation workflows.

business_outcome: DXC-Luxoft says the application lets non-experts create simulator-executable driving scenarios from natural-language descriptions, enabling more scalable virtual validation while saving time, lowering costs, and reducing reliance on scarce domain specialists.
